usage: wsp computers
  your computers: this Mac, each box you added, with what each has, whether it
  is connected, how many machines it holds and what runs there against its cap

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp computers set <computer> [--name <new>] [--ssh <login>]
       [--threads <n>] [--machines <n>] [--spend <usd>] [--size <cpu>x<memGb>]
       [--delete-after <minutes>] [--nap <minutes>|off]
       [--turn-limit <hours>|off] [--max-machines <n>] [--max-depth <n>]
       [--recipe <name>|none] [--reset <setting>]...
  what you set on one of your computers: its name, the ssh login it is reached
  by, how many threads run there at once, how long a quiet machine there runs
  before it naps, how long one turn there may run, the caps on agents starting
  agents, the recipe it follows, and on a cloud how many machines at once, how
  much it spends a day, the size a sub-thread's machine gets and how long a
  finished one stays; --reset takes a setting back to its default

  --name            what to call a computer you added from now, which every
                    listing then shows; its id, its projects and its machines
                    stay as they are
  --ssh             the login user@host the host reaches a computer you added by
                    over ssh from now, saved only once the computer it reaches
                    reads as that same one
  --threads         how many threads may run on that computer at once; a new one
                    waits past it
  --machines        how many machines may run on that cloud at once
  --spend           the dollars a day that cloud may spend before it starts no
                    new machine
  --size            on a cloud, the size a sub-thread's machine gets when the
                    thread starting it names none, as <cpu>x<memGb>; 2x4 until
                    it is set
  --delete-after    on a cloud, the minutes a finished sub-thread's machine
                    stays before it is deleted, 0 to 1440; 30 until it is set
  --nap             the minutes a quiet machine there runs before it naps, or
                    off
  --turn-limit      the hours one turn there may run before it is stopped, or
                    off; off on a computer you own until it is set
  --max-machines    how many machines may stand at once under one root thread;
                    defaults to 3
  --max-depth       how many levels of threads may stand under the root thread;
                    defaults to 2
  --recipe          the saved recipe it follows from now, by the name wsp
                    recipes shows, or none to keep what it has and follow
                    nothing
  --reset           a setting to take back to its default, by its flag's word;
                    repeats
  --json            print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line,
                    with everything else on stderr
  --state           the state file the host serves
  --host            run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp
                    hosts lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp recipes
  your saved recipes: what each puts on a computer in one line, and the
  computers that follow it

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp recipes show <name>
  one recipe whole: every row it holds by kind, the computers that follow it,
  and the hash it resolves to on this computer now

  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp recipes save <name> --from <computer>
  saves what one of your computers was set up with as a recipe under that name,
  and that computer follows it from then on

  --from     the computer whose picks the recipe is saved from, by the name wsp
             computers shows; it follows the recipe from then on
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp recipes remove <name> [--yes]
  takes a recipe away; the computers that followed it keep what they have and
  follow none

  --yes      go ahead without being asked
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp usage [--range day|week|month]
       [--by agent|account|computer|project|model|source]
  what each agent account signed in on any of your computers may still use, and
  what was used over a day, a week or a month split one way, the work your
  agents logged outside wsp counted with wsp's threads as on the Usage page
  (--by source shows how much is outside); two answers, never added together

  --range    the days what was used is read over: day (today, the default), week
             (the last seven) or month (the last thirty); the accounts' limits
             are the same whatever it says
  --by       how what was used is split: agent (the default), account, computer,
             project or model
  --json     print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
             everything else on stderr
  --state    the state file the host serves
  --host     run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
             lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell

usage: wsp usage reset <account> [--credit <id>] [--on <computer>] [--yes]
  spends one of the resets a Codex account has banked, on a computer of yours
  that holds its login, after reading the account there: its five-hour and
  weekly windows start again now; asks first unless --yes

  --credit    the reset to spend, by the id Codex lists it under; whichever
              Codex picks without it
  --on        the computer to spend it on, by the name wsp computers shows, one
              of the account's own that holds its login; the first of those that
              is connected without it
  --yes       go ahead without being asked
  --json      print the raw protocol values, one JSON object per line, with
              everything else on stderr
  --state     the state file the host serves
  --host      run the line against a host on your account, by the name wsp hosts
              lists it under; WSP_HOST names one for a whole shell
